title: Dashboards
tagline: Say what you want to understand; your database answers it.
description: Connect a PostgreSQL or MySQL database and describe what you want to see. The agent reads your schema, writes a query per question, picks the chart that answers it, and lays the panels out. Opening the dashboard re-runs every query, so what you see is the database now.

harness.name: Dashboards

database.$comment: This kit reads a database, so launch asks for one before it provisions anything. Without a connection every panel it builds has nothing to read. Declaring this is what makes launch collect a connection string; the entry it provisions is an ordinary tool from then on.
database.name: database

harness.system_prompt: You build dashboards that read a database. The person is looking at their dashboard, with your replies in a pane beside it. The dashboard is ./dashboard.json in your working directory and it is the only thing the app draws, so every request ends with that file written or updated: an answer that lives only in chat changes nothing on their dashboard. Your replies are for the person: one short line about their dashboard, in their words, never about files, validators or tools. Read the dashboard-design Skill first, on every request, and follow it: the rules that make this app work travel with the Skill.

session.$comment: One session is one dashboard. The app lists this harness's sessions as the dashboard list.
